introduction: Some twenty thousand Bábís and Bahá’ís were killed for their faith in nineteenth-century Persia, and killings continued in the twentieth. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá wrote prayers for many of them by name, and prayers of visitation to be said at their graves. This guide gathers them with Bahá’u’lláh’s and the Báb’s. They ask that the martyr be raised, sheltered and made a star; that the family be comforted and confirmed; that the suppliant be helped by the martyr’s merit; and sometimes that the one praying be given the same cup. The Apocalypse’s souls under the altar and multitude in white, the Wisdom of Solomon’s “souls of the righteous”, the Qur’an’s “think not of them as dead” and Stephen’s death are the scriptures of martyrdom; Lincoln at Gettysburg spoke of what the living owe the dead, and Owen of deaths that no prayer dignified.
questions: What do these prayers ask for the dead, what for the bereaved, and what for the one praying?
The martyrs of the Apocalypse cry for judgment. What do these prayers ask in the martyrs’ name instead?
Lincoln said the living must take up “the unfinished work”. How do readings 59 and 60 say the same?
Several prayers ask for the cup of martyrdom. How can that be prayed honestly by someone living in safety?

outside.why: Thy martyred servant feared not the threats. Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints.
Glorify the abode of this newly arrived guest. In my Father’s house are many mansions: I go to prepare a place for you.
Make the grieving family joyful. Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.

“I beseech Thee by them and by their blood.” The souls under the altar cried, how long, O Lord, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood? John’s martyrs ask for judgment; the reading asks, by the martyrs’ blood, for relief and mercy.
Make him a star rising in the highest horizon. They that turn many to righteousness shall shine as the stars for ever and ever.
Shelter him in the cave of Thy grace. He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
For spending his spirit. Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.
Crowned with the crown of faithfulness. I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith.
Clothe them with the robe of Thy favour. These are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes.
Whoso is martyred in the path of God, God will exalt. Think not of those who are slain in the way of Allah as dead. Nay, they are living.
Blessings on the bodies that suffered. The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God; in the sight of the unwise they seemed to die.
By their steadfastness and the pieces of their bodies. Stephen, dying, prayed for those who stoned him: Lord, lay not this sin to their charge.
Accept from Thy loved ones their spilled blood. Judas Maccabeus prayed for his fallen soldiers, for if he had not hoped that they should rise again, it had been superfluous to pray for the dead.

“Withhold not from me what Thou hast ordained for them.” Whosoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it. Jesus also told the persecuted to flee from city to city. How should a prayer to be given martyrdom be said by people who are not asked to die?
May the Concourse on High visit those spirits. Seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us run with patience the race.
Words to be said at a martyr’s tomb. Lincoln at a field of graves: the world will little note what we say here, but it can never forget what they did here.

Blessed is the one who visits your resting place. Owen on the dead of another kind of slaughter: what passing-bells for these who die as cattle? Only the monstrous anger of the guns. What separates a death the readings call martyrdom from the deaths he mourns?
Confirm the relatives of these martyrs in serving. It is for us the living, rather, to be dedicated here to the unfinished work.
The offspring of that noble band. A father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows, is God in his holy habitation.

shortfall: The sixty prayers ask the same mercies, for one martyr after another, in nearly the same words; a companion was set at each distinct petition.
